title: Enterprise Ask Origami: multi-account intake & initial feasibility canvas
creator: Priya Singh
description: Consolidate a backlog of high-touch enterprise feature asks from Sales/CS into a single prioritized intake canvas (the 'Origami' artifact). The goal is to produce a consumable synthesis that: 1) groups similar asks across accounts, 2) surfaces functional/tech commonalities, 3) produces initial feasibility (engineering effort, infra impact, security/compliance flags), and 4) recommends whether to: a) fold into an existing roadmap item, b) scope a narrow pilot, or c) reject/defer. This ticket is the product-scoped first pass to standardize the aggregation + scoring pipeline and handoff format for Eng/Design/Legal/Revenue partners.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page Origami canvas exists in Drive summarizing at least 7 recent enterprise asks grouped into 3 hypothesis clusters
Each cluster has: representative customer examples, estimated dev effort (T-shirt), major infra dependencies, security/compliance flags, and recommended next action (roadmap/pilot/defer)
Stakeholder readout completed with CS lead, 2 AEs, Eng owner, and Privacy/Legal; feedback captured in comments and incorporated
Scoring rubric documented (value/earnings probability/implementation risk) and validated on three historical asks to show expected prioritization stability
Handoff template (Confluence + Linear quick-create fields) published so CS can submit future bundles using the same format
comments: 2026-02-20 | Priya Singh: Kickoff — pulled CS ask exports for last 9 months. Initial clustering shows 3 dominant themes: account-scoped throttling controls, per-tenant model pinning, and audit log export formats.

2026-02-25 | Diego Ramirez: Eng feasibility quickscan — per-tenant model pinning looks medium effort but high infra cost due to separate model versions + storage for KV caches. Suggested alternative: routing-based pinning to model variants to limit infra growth.

2026-03-01 | Ava Kim (CS): Confirmed 7 prioritized customer asks to include; supplied revenue estimates for 4 accounts. Noted that two security-sensitive customers require HSM-backed keying for embeddings — mark security flag.
2026-03-04 | Marco Chen (Legal): Legal flagged one cluster (log export for regulated customers) as needing data residency proof; recommendation: include Private deployment option in pilot scoping.
2026-03-08 | Diego Ramirez: Added initial scoring rubric to canvas (Value: 1-5, Probability: 1-5, Risk: 1-5). Early runs show highest score for 'per-tenant rate limits + quota controls'.
2026-03-12 | Priya Singh: Readout scheduled with GTM and Eng on 2026-03-14. Draft PRD and Confluence handoff template posted (see links). Seeking decision on pilot vs roadmap merge for top cluster.

2026-03-14 | Diego Ramirez: Readout complete. Stakeholders lean to: pilot for quota controls (pilot w/ 2 accounts), roadmap ticket for model pinning (broader architecture work), and defer granular log export to Private deployment initiative. Updated canvas per feedback. Moving to In Review.
decision_summary: Split outcome: 1) Quota/tenant rate-limiting -> pilot with 2 anchor accounts (low infra risk, high immediate revenue). 2) Per-tenant model pinning -> architectural epic for Dedicated/Private (high infra cost; requires kernel/runtime changes). 3) Audit/log export formats -> align with Private deployment roadmap and data residency controls. Legal/Privacy to own compliance checklist for pilot.

Create PM-24811: Architecture epic scoping for model pinning (input to ENG-92114)
Assign Legal checklist owner and confirm HSM/KMS constraints for pilot accounts
Publish Confluence handoff template and update CS intake form to require revenue signal and compliance flags
